messages.subject: can someone explain this?
parts:
Hi all-

I do not get the expected behavior from llply in the last line. 

Thanks in advance. 
James

> list(a=NULL, b=NULL)
$a
NULL

$b
NULL

> list(a=NULL, b=NULL)[[1]]
NULL

> list(a=NULL, b=NULL)[[2]]
NULL

> is.null(list(a=NULL, b=NULL)[[1]])
[1] TRUE

> is.null(list(a=NULL, b=NULL)[[2]])
[1] TRUE

> llply( list(a=NULL, b=NULL), '[[', is.null)

$a
NULL

$b
NULL

--

messages.author: e531efa2753b204e
messages.subject: Re: can someone explain this?
parts:
just llply( list(a=NULL, b=NULL), is.null ) works. The ‘[[' is done by llply (it’s what the first “L” indicates)

d <- list(a=NULL, b=NULL)
llply( d, is.null ) #equivalent to list(is.null(d[[1]]), is.null(d[[2]]))
llply( d, `[[`, is.null) #equivalent to list( d[[1]][[is.null]], d[[2]][[is.null]] )

Peter
